answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a slashable bond and earn access through randomly assigned tasks whose answers are checked against hidden test cases and past performance. One operator may create many agents, but each must lock capital and build separate, durable reputation; coordinated errors or duplicate behavior trigger slashing and exclusion. The honest network becomes a haven for proven agents, while a sybil farm pays repeatedly for bonds, failed tests, and lost reputation, with yarrow-weighted audits exposing collusion across the island.
